methods.title: Observe
methods.question: What is actually happening?
methods.description: Describe the symptom, the affected workflow, and the evidence available before proposing an explanation.

methods.title: Investigate
methods.question: What would disprove the hypothesis?
methods.description: Connect observations, establish a timeline, and distinguish what is known from what is assumed.

methods.title: Build
methods.question: What is the smallest useful change?
methods.description: Choose a focused approach with explicit boundaries and clear handling of failure.

methods.title: Validate
methods.question: How will we know it works?
methods.description: Check expected behaviour, edge cases and the recovery path. Evaluate against the original problem.

methods.title: Operate
methods.question: Can someone understand and support it?
methods.description: Think about visibility, maintainability, documentation and the people responsible for the system.

methods.title: Improve
methods.question: What should become easier next time?
methods.description: Use feedback to simplify the next iteration and make useful learning repeatable.

notes.title: Before the fix, find the signal.
notes.summary: A short framework for evidence-led incident investigation.

sections.heading: Establish a timeline
sections.text: Record the symptom and the relevant changes. A timeline is more useful than a collection of unrelated observations.

sections.heading: Separate evidence from interpretation
sections.text: Write down what you know and what you are inferring. Ask which observation could disprove your current explanation.

sections.heading: Check the recovery
sections.text: A disappearing error is one signal. Verify the original workflow and document what remains uncertain.

notes.note: New editorial draft prepared for this portfolio. Not a previously published article or an account of a specific employer incident.

notes.title: Explain it by building it.
notes.summary: Making a technical idea tangible through a small feedback loop.

sections.heading: Start with a visible behaviour
sections.text: Use a simple input and output, such as a sensor changing an indicator. Make the causal relationship observable.

sections.heading: Change one thing
sections.text: Let the learner predict the effect of a small change, then compare the result with that prediction.

sections.heading: Name the underlying idea
sections.text: Connect the observation to the concept after the learner has something concrete to reason about.

notes.note: New educational draft prepared for this portfolio, informed by the résumé’s robotics teaching background. Not a claimed published lesson.
